html:
SMTO-EXE-0094 — SMTO can't read text on that computer

GUID: 33552462-0ec6-51b2-9e1b-6cf38966e2e3
Slug: screen-ocr-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • Reading text from a screenshot or image needs a text-reading program called Tesseract on the Gateway's computer. It's missing there, or it doesn't have the language you asked for. Taking screenshots still works.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked SMTO to read a language other than English, try English first, or have that language added to Tesseract on that computer. SMTO can only read languages whose Tesseract language files are installed there.
  2. If English also fails, run the Gateway installer again on that computer when no task is using it. Don't delete the Gateway first. The installer puts back Tesseract and its English data if they are missing.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a New chat and ask again. Existing chats keep the Gateway's old list of abilities; a new chat sees that text reading works.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the text it read from the screen or image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the language you need, to the person who installed the Gateway. Turning on the Screen skill doesn't install Tesseract or any language files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OCR readiness could not find or run Tesseract, the requested language data is not installed, or searchable-PDF generation found a Tesseract version older than 4.

What this means

  • OCR readiness could not locate or query Tesseract, lacked requested language data, or found an unsupported engine version for searchable PDF generation. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • OCR readiness could not locate or query Tesseract, lacked requested language data, or found an unsupported engine version for searchable PDF generation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect installed engine/version and language metadata; distinguish failed language discovery from definitely missing language files.

How to fix it

  • If Tesseract or its eng data is missing, rerun the Gateway's supported installer in place, restart the Gateway once active work has settled and refresh its capabilities. For another OCR language, install that Tesseract language data on the selected Gateway and confirm it with tesseract --list-langs. Searchable PDF output needs Tesseract 4 or later.
  • If Tesseract or its English data is missing, reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. For another requested OCR language, install that language data on the selected Gateway and verify it is listed by tesseract --list-langs. Screen capture itself does not require OCR.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • The local engine reports the required language and supported version, then completes an explicit OCR request.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
